children: Gold futures fall for a third straight session as the U.S. dollar strengthens and Treasury yields rise, including the 10-year yield at its highest level since July 2007. Fed officials have reaffirmed support for last week's interest-rate increase while warning of inflation risks, sustaining odds above 50% of another rate increase in October, Critical Metals' CEO Tony Sage says in a note. "A firmer U.S. dollar and elevated U.S. yields could also continue to keep pressure on bullion." Front-month gold falls 1.3% in New York to $4,281.30 a troy ounce. Silver settles down 2.4% at $64.382 a troy ounce. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
